_about: Registry of bugs this codebase has produced MORE THAN ONCE. Each entry is an automatic check (tools/check_known_bugs.py) that runs on every push and PR and turns the run red with the bug id and file:line. Owner's rule, 2026-09-11: a bug seen twice gets a checker; a red checker is fixed before anything else. Add an entry the second time you meet a bug, with both sightings.

bugs.title: Windows line endings in a file that runs on the server
bugs.why: A shell script, systemd unit or nginx config edited on Windows and committed with CRLF fails on the box in ways that look unrelated: `$'\r': command not found`, a systemd unit that will not parse, an rclone key with a trailing carriage return ('invalid key or value contains \n or \r').
seen: 2026-09-11 14:10 the whole deploy/vps kit needed a sed pass before its first run
2026-09-11 16:30 the same again for the retention scripts
2026-09-11 17:52 a carriage return rode along in the Backblaze key pipe and rclone refused it
bugs.fix: save the file with LF (the repo's .gitattributes now forces it for these paths); `sed -i 's/\r$//' <file>`

bugs.title: Em dash or en dash in source, docs or deploy files
bugs.why: Hard rule (owner 2026-07-13): never an em dash or en dash anywhere. They read as machine-written and the owner has asked for their removal repeatedly.
seen: 2026-08-03: 2,427 removed across roughly 300 files in both repos
2026-09-04: the design lint found six more that had crept back in
bugs.fix: a hyphen with spaces, a comma, a colon, parentheses, or reword

bugs.title: A script edits .env with a `^KEY=` anchor, but the production .env writes `KEY = value`
bugs.why: The AWS .env, and therefore the VPS one, has spaces around `=` for every line. A sed or grep anchored on `^KEY=` silently matches nothing, the old value stays, and the failure surfaces later as 'Access denied for user admin@localhost'. (Only the Django .env has this shape; afcbot/.env is plain KEY=value, so its keys are not in the pattern.)
seen: 2026-09-11 13:40 05-env-and-venv.sh was written with `^DB_USER=` and had to be rewritten before its first run
2026-09-11 15:33 the cutover re-sync restored the AWS .env and the DB lines had to be re-applied by hand with the loose pattern
bugs.fix: anchor as `^\s*KEY\s*=` and write back in the same `KEY = value` style

bugs.title: A validator's sentence is unpacked into `message`, overwriting what the user wrote
bugs.why: `is_valid, message = is_valid_email(email)` looks harmless, and inside contact_us it overwrote the visitor's own `message` two lines before the email body was built. Every Contact Us mail AFC received for months read `Message: Valid email.`, while the sender was told it had been sent. Nothing failed, nothing logged, and the words were gone. The validator's result must have its own name (`email_error`), because `message` is the name request payloads use for the thing a human typed.
seen: 2026-09-14 the owner: "the only email we get in our email is 'valid email'" - every contact message since the form shipped
2026-09-14 five more call sites in afc_auth/views.py were one user-typed field away from the same fault, and were renamed with it
bugs.fix: name the validator's second value `email_error`; never unpack a validator into `message`

bugs.title: A view answers the client with str(e) of a caught exception
bugs.why: The exception text reaches the client (MySQL sentences, paths, implementation hints: best-practice rule 21) and NOTHING reaches the journal, so a 500 real people hit twenty times had to be diagnosed from the byte count of the response body (inbox #23, /team/send-join-request/, 2026-09-17). Log it, answer a plain sentence with a code.
seen: 2026-09-16: /team/send-join-request/ answered 500 {"error": "(1406, Data too long for column 'message')"} 13 times to two people; no traceback anywhere
2026-09-17: six more sites of the same shape in afc_team/views.py, rewritten to _internal_error
bugs.fix: logger.exception(...) and Response({"message": "An error occurred.", "code": "internal_error"}, status=500); in afc_team/views.py use _internal_error(e, "<view>")
